mathematical_sources.location: Public repository enaslund/unit-distance-bound-0.0427: papers/0.043171/ at the cited commit (main.tex, sections/, certificates/). The source archive includes the manuscript, its research README and the external evidence for (H_W) (certificates/dihedral/h_w_receipt.py and .json) under docs/research-1.043171/.
mathematical_sources.note: Self-contained manuscript of October 8, 2026, for the 41-cap tower over Q(sqrt 241): the tower with the Frobenius cap moved from the prime 7 to a prime above 41, the dihedral quotients of the tower group, the field E_W of degree 8192 (the paper's E_{W''}) and the factorization of its zeta function, the bound for the relative zeta value, the geometric construction and the proof of the main theorem. It proves the exponent 1.043171 unconditionally, with a computer-assisted certificate; this formalization proves the exponent 1.04315 conditional on the displayed hypothesis (H_W), with a single abscissa in place of the paper's census to 4e13, signed kernel and general shell weights. Independent AI referee reviews found no error affecting the theorem. It is an unrefereed manuscript produced with AI tools under Eric Naslund's direction, with an AI Methodology statement on its first page; it is not a peer-reviewed publication. His role as directing author and responsible maintainer does not assert human proof review. No registry action is claimed by this metadata.

mathematical_sources.note: Self-contained manuscript of September 30, 2026, revised for readability on October 1, 2026, with the interval corrections of its certificates of October 2, 2026, for the tower over Q(sqrt 241) with the Frobenius cap at the prime 7: the tower, the Kummer field of the tower (called the genus field here) and its 255 quadratic L-functions, the upper bound for the relative zeta value, the geometric construction and the proof of the main theorem. It proves the exponent 1.04273 unconditionally, with a computer-assisted certificate. Version 1 of this formalization proved the exponent 1.0427 conditional on an inequality (H241) for the genus field; version 2 reuses its tower, genus field, analytic machinery and geometric construction with the changes of the 1.043171 paper. It is an unrefereed manuscript produced with AI tools under Eric Naslund's direction, with an AI Methodology statement on its first page, published in the repository cited above; it is not a peer-reviewed publication. No registry action is claimed by this metadata.

related_formalizations.note: Registered on 2026-10-01 from public commit e0ac836176016dbefae28646bc91fc3a5aca30e8 of enaslund/unit-distance-bound-0.0427: the planar sequence theorem at exponent 10427/10000 conditional on the inequality H241 for the genus field E (target_of_canonical_genus_zeta_bound). The present formalization keeps the repository, the project path and the comparator configuration path, changes the tower (cap above 41 instead of at 7), the comparison field (E_W of degree 8192 instead of E), the exponent and the selected theorem (target_of_wide_zeta_bound), and removes the endpoint modules of the 1.0427 theorem.
related_formalizations.relationship: builds-on (the earlier formalization of the 1.0427 theorem, from the same repository)

related_formalizations.note: The library of the verified conditional 1.0418235 package (Lean v4.35.0-rc2) is reused unchanged: generic geometry, analysis, class field theory ports and pro-p machinery are imported; witness-dependent modules are copied into UnitDistance/Sqrt241 with the new data (generator scripts in scripts/sqrt241/), and the Q tower is rebuilt over Q(sqrt 241). This identifies the local research revision merged into this branch. Its selected 1.0418235 archive passed two bounded full local runs; those passes do not verify the new 1.0427 theorem. The 1.0418235 theorem remains in the same Lean project (ChallengeZeta/SolutionZeta). Its public-layout candidate was prepared locally and remains unpublished and unregistered; the sqrt241 package is the intended submission. No public identifier for that formalization is asserted here.

Matched dependency target for Lean v4.35.0-rc2, Apache-2.0. Exact selected-build and archive-verification outcomes require receipts for the corresponding source and archive digests. Its own pinned dependencies remain external public dependencies.

Formal Frontier Team, Apache-2.0. Its multidimensional Poisson summation module (DedekindZeta/PoissonSummation.lean) is version-ported, with original copyright/license and explicit modification provenance, to UnitDistance/ThirdParty/PoissonSummation.lean; the full source file compiled against the present pinned Mathlib, and PoissonBound derives translated finite lattice bounds from actual dual Fourier tails. The ideal-series, geometric-product and factorization sections of DedekindZeta/Statements.lean are ported into DedekindEuler, and selected trace-dual proofs from DedekindZeta/Theta.lean into MinkowskiTrace; those two modules carry the sum_product adaptations in this package. EulerBound.lean through its divisor-series theorem is ported into IdealCounting in the research repository, but the IdealCounting port named in NOTICE is not in this package's selected import closure. Original copyright and license are preserved and modifications and the new full Euler-product assembly are recorded in docs/SUBMISSION_PROVENANCE.md and NOTICE. The whole upstream project was not rebuilt; other code was audited at source level. Its field tower is an explicit hypothesis. License retained under third-party/sum_product/LICENSE. No registration of that project is claimed.

Chris Birkbeck, Apache-2.0. Completed Dedekind zeta and explicit-formula foundations are ported as an attributed source port under UnitDistance/Upstream/AINTLIB. Copyright, license, exact source hashes and version modifications are recorded in third-party/aintlib. Completed zeta continuation and functional equation are actual theorems; relative Hecke entireness is not assumed to follow.

Naganori Yamaguchi, Apache-2.0. Selected profinite presentations and continuous pro-p cohomology are imported under UnitDistance/Upstream/Yamaguchi, retaining original declaration namespaces and mathematical statements. The selected archive inventory records which files of the larger historical port are shipped. License, original/local source hashes, compatibility patches and dated verification scope are in third-party/yamaguchi. Historical build and imported-axiom-query records retain their original scope and are not a verifier result for the new theorem. New local arithmetic proofs assemble the seven-relation bound over Q(sqrt 241) and the growing field family; those conclusions are not supplied as upstream assumptions.

Erdős unit-distance formalization contributors, Apache-2.0. Selected openNormalChain and fixed-field construction proofs from ErdosUnitDistance/Internal/ClassFieldTheory/Witness.lean are adapted in ProfiniteQuotientTower and GaloisQuotientTower. License, NOTICE, hashes and modifications are retained under third-party/erdos-unit-distance. The whole upstream project was not rebuilt. No upstream arithmetic tower or headline theorem is assumed; its unspecified-exponent theorem and explicit odd-prime Shafarevich and Golod-Shafarevich inputs do not supply the present dyadic tower. No registration of that project is claimed.

Tristen Harr, Apache-2.0. Twelve generic entire-function and canonical Hadamard product modules and a selected negation-pairing section are ported, with original headers and exact provenance under third-party/entire-hadamard. No xi-specific module or Riemann Hypothesis assumption is imported. New local compositions derive paired-product monotonicity from actual entire divisor, summability and growth data.

Registered in the Palomar registry as PALOMAR-2026-08-08-000001 (2026-08-08); a Comparator wrapper for the library kim-em/erdos-unit-distance at 34b4587bbd0740efb9c06a519a8ee14a3eff8cd7. It proves the uniform-constant form of the disproof of the Erdős unit-distance conjecture (for every C > 0, arbitrarily large n admit n-point planar sets with more than n^(1 + C/log log n) unit-distance pairs), a different and weaker statement than the fixed exponent here. No code or theorem from it is used.

Independent Lean formalization of the fixed-power (unspecified-exponent) planar unit-distance statement, as described in the Palomar record PALOMAR-2026-08-08-000001. No code or theorem from it is used, and no comparison of exponents is claimed.
